title: Data Scale, Not Latency, Shapes Cross-Lingual Encoder Transfer in Streaming ASR
abstract: arXiv:2606.24169v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Adapting a streaming speech recognition model to a new language requires choosing between two plausible warm starts: a multilingual (ML) encoder or an English-only (EN) encoder. The common intuition is that the multilingual encoder should help most at low data, but it is unclear how long that advantage persists, whether tight streaming latency amplifies it, and whether it survives deployment quantization. We answer these questions with a controlled sweep of a 0.6 B-parameter cache-aware FastConformer transducer across eight European languages, up to five target-language data scales (100 h to 2500 h), three streaming tiers plus offline decoding, and up to four public test sets. The main result is that multilingual initialization is a data-limited advantage, not a latency-limited one. On FLEURS at 160 ms, the mean EN-ML word error rate (WER) gap falls from +4.21 percentage points (pp) at 100 h to +0.20 pp at 2500 h; a power-law fit sum

translated_title: 数据规模而非延迟决定了流式语音识别中跨语言编码器的迁移
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.24169v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：将流式语音识别模型适配到新语言时，需要在两种合理的预热启动方案之间做出选择：多语言（ML）编码器或仅英语（EN）编码器。通常的直觉是多语言编码器在低数据量时帮助最大，但不清楚这种优势能持续多久、严格的流式延迟是否会放大该优势，以及它能否在部署量化后得以保留。我们通过对一个0.6B参数的缓存感知FastConformer传感器模型进行系统性控制实验来回答这些问题，实验涵盖八种欧洲语言、最多五个目标语言数据规模（100小时至2500小时）、三个流式延迟层级加上离线解码，以及最多四个公开测试集。主要结论是：多语言初始化带来的优势是受数据量限制的，而非受延迟限制的。在FLEURS测试集160毫秒延迟下，EN与ML之间的平均词错误率（WER）差距从100小时数据时的+4.21个百分点下降到2500小时数据时的+0.20个百分点；幂律拟合……
tldr: 本研究通过对0.6B参数流式FastConformer模型在八种欧洲语言、多个数据规模和延迟层级上的系统实验，发现多语言编码器初始化带来的优势是受数据量限制的而非受流式延迟限制的——随着目标语言训练数据从100小时增至2500小时，其相对仅英语编码器的WER优势从+4.21个百分点缩小至+0.20个百分点。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates through controlled experiments on a 0.6B-parameter cache-aware FastConformer transducer across eight European languages that multilingual encoder initialization provides a data-limited, not latency-limited, advantage, with the EN-ML WER gap shrinking from +4.21pp at 100h to +0.20pp at 2500h of target-language training data.
